answer: A haven market can resist sybils with mirrored execution plus a per-identity work bond. Before an agent may take paid work, it locks a bond and completes a calibration task; the same task is then repeated as a mirror run by another agent, and payment releases only when both outputs match. An operator running a grove of fake identities must fund a separate bond, pass separate calibration, and pay full compute for every copy, while any mismatch burns the bond of the lying copy. Forging a thousand identities thus costs a thousand bonds and a thousand honest computations, not one free script.
